clue.text: Al Pacino's tip for modifying smartphone features?

indicators.note: modifying means changing, so the letters before it are to be altered into a new order

blocks.note: the actor's name, the possessive S and the word tip, all taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A film star offers advice on customising the features of a phone.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is not a possessive here: its S joins the fodder along with every letter of the actor's name and the word tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Apps, the programs installed on a phone, are short for applications, which is what gives the handset its features.

clue.text: Old man knocked over friend, creating outrage

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up upside down, which in a down entry means read from the bottom up

blocks.note: an informal word for father
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone causes a scandal by knocking a friend over in a fight with an old man.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to shock or fill with dismay, the same as to outrage someone as a verb.

clue.text: Poor swan on ship circling African river

indicators.note: circling means going around, so the ship's letters surround the river's name

blocks.note: a pen is a female swan
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
the great river of north-east Africa

explanation.surface: A poor swan rides on a boat cruising round the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' means placed above, so the swan comes first and the ship-around-river follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Penniless means having no money at all, so it is a synonym for poor.

clue.text: Criminal under the weather — for example, Capone?

blocks.note: feeling unwell
the abbreviation of the Latin exempli gratia
the gangster Al Capone's first name

explanation.surface: A gangster such as Capone is described as a criminal who is feeling poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, criminal means against the law, a synonym of unlawful.

clue.text: Artificial human as well as French fashion designer turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: and means as well as
Christian Dior, the Paris couturier

explanation.surface: A robot shows up alongside a famous French couturier.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a robot built to look and behave like a person, in science fiction especially.

clue.text: Couple I encountered heading north

indicators.note: heading north in a down entry means travelling upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
met means encountered

explanation.surface: Someone recalls meeting a pair travelling northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a couple in a romantic relationship, as in 'they are an item'.

clue.text: More insensitive, half-hearted teen in official residence

indicators.note: half of the heart is lost, so one of the two central letters drops out

blocks.note: more numb, the comparative of numb
taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: A rather unfeeling teenager is living in an official residence.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER here is pronounced num-er, more numb, not the counting word. The middle of the word has two E's, and losing one is half its heart. Number Ten Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's London home.
explanation.definitionFit: Number Ten Downing Street is where the British Prime Minister officially lives, so it is a government residence.

clue.text: Secretly listen to hesitant remark about a toupee

indicators.note: about means around, so the hesitation goes around the single letter

blocks.note: the sound of hesitation
taken as written
a toupee is a small wig

explanation.surface: Someone eavesdrops on an awkward comment about a man's hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is an informal British verb for eavesdropping on someone else's conversation.

clue.text: International organisation's support is tacit

blocks.note: the UN, the United Nations, plus the possessive S
aid means help or support

explanation.surface: Backing from a world body is given implicitly rather than openly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsaid is understood without being spoken, which is what tacit means.

clue.text: Tree snake seen regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every second letter is kept

blocks.note: an asp is a venomous snake
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A snake is spotted in a tree every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar tree known for its trembling leaves.

clue.text: Flirtatious fellows send email that's rewritten

indicators.note: something rewritten has its words reworked, so the letters are to be rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Womanisers send a message that has been redrafted.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' man is a man who enjoys the company of women and flirts with them.

clue.text: Famous duke with a famous Duke

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
Duke Ellington, the American jazz bandleader

explanation.surface: One celebrated aristocrat appears alongside another.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital D marks the second 'Duke' as a first name: the jazz musician, not a nobleman. The first is the Duke of Wellington, who beat Napoleon at Waterloo.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Duke of Wellington, the soldier and Prime Minister, is the best-known holder of any British dukedom.

clue.text: Greek character going after fine Greek food

indicators.note: going after means following, so the letter comes second, behind the abbreviation

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person pursues some good Greek cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white cheese from Greece, made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Refined chap accompanying slippery customer

indicators.note: accompanying means going along with, so the two parts sit side by side

blocks.note: short for gentleman
an eel is slippery, and the phrase also means a shifty person

explanation.surface: A polished man is out with a shifty character.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel means polite and refined in manner, often affectedly so.

clue.text: Pan actors playing for absolutely nothing

indicators.note: players move around a stage, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The cast of Peter Pan are performing without being paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a scrap is an idiom for none at all, nothing whatsoever.

clue.text: Loyal Democrat cast a ballot to save energy

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe inside, so the earlier letters enclose the extra one

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
voted means cast a ballot
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A faithful Democrat goes out to vote in an effort to conserve power.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoted means deeply committed and faithful to someone, a synonym of loyal.

clue.text: Clubs with right-wingers supporting five-one wins

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath, so those letters go after

blocks.note: Roman numerals for five and one
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
Tories are members of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Football clubs backed by right-wing fans win five-one.
explanation.walkthrough: Five-one reads like a scoreline, but it gives two Roman numerals. Tories is the everyday name for British Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Victories are wins, successes in a contest or battle.

clue.text: Excerpt from Mozart is a number for a skilful person

indicators.note: an excerpt is a passage taken out of a longer piece, so the letters are found within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the composer's name to the start of the last word

explanation.surface: A passage from a Mozart piece is a song suited to a talented musician.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled craftsman who makes things by hand.

clue.text: Travel in a North American city or country in Africa

indicators.note: in places the travelling word inside the string of letters that follows it

blocks.note: taken as written
the compass abbreviation
to go is to travel
Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Should you go to a city in North America or travel to Africa?
explanation.walkthrough: 'North American city' reads as one phrase, but North and American city are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Angola is a nation on the south-western coast of Africa, a former Portuguese colony.

clue.text: Rear end of Raducanu caught by return shot

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of the following name is used
something shot is wrecked, so the word before it is scrambled
something caught by another is held within it

blocks.note: the final letter of the tennis player's surname
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Emma Raducanu's backside is struck by a ball coming back over the net.
explanation.walkthrough: Emma Raducanu is a British tennis player, and 'return shot' sounds like a tennis stroke, but shot is the anagram signal. Rear is a verb here, not a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear a child is to bring it up and care for it, so nurture is a synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Supports commanding officer in dispatches

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word that follows

blocks.note: to dispatch is to send
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone backs a commander mentioned in military reports.
explanation.walkthrough: Mentioned in dispatches is a military honour, but dispatches is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a motion or proposal is to back it formally, so seconds means supports.

clue.text: Poet getting into novels pens erotica

indicators.note: getting into means going inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle all three words

explanation.surface: A poet who starts writing fiction produces racy material.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Dodgy lovers for you?

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The setter teases the reader about having untrustworthy partners.
explanation.definitionFit: The person reading and working out this clue is the crossword solver, so 'you' names them.

clue.text: Augustus and Henry initially speak effusively

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the king's name is kept

blocks.note: Gus is the short form of the name
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Two Roman or royal figures begin to talk enthusiastically.
explanation.definitionFit: To gush is to talk with excessive enthusiasm or praise, pouring out words.

clue.text: Chaotic brawl? No one is charged

blocks.note: first meaning: a disorganised fight in which everyone joins in
second meaning, read literally: there is no charge for anyone

explanation.surface: A disorderly fight in which nobody ends up being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: Charged looks like a police term, but the second reading is about price: everything costs nothing to everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for an unruly melee, and taken literally means something available at no cost to everyone.

clue.text: Case of Americans welcoming flipping crazy US president

indicators.note: a case is the outside covering, so only the outer letters of the next word are used
flipping turns something over, so the word is read backwards
welcoming means taking in, so the outer letters hold the turned word

blocks.note: first and last letters
mad means crazy

explanation.surface: Americans welcome a wildly unhinged president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads like a mild British swear word meaning very, but it signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and John Quincy Adams were the second and sixth presidents of the United States.

clue.text: Heartless oafs look for European capital

indicators.note: without a heart the middle letters go, keeping only the outside pair

blocks.note: first and last letters
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Unfeeling louts go in search of a European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: After fun escapade, Tottenham making bloomers

indicators.note: after places the football club's name behind the escapade

blocks.note: a lark is a bit of fun or a prank
the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, the London football club

explanation.surface: After a prank, Tottenham Hotspur's players make embarrassing blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers looks like blunders or old-fashioned knickers, but here it means things that bloom: flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspurs are flowering plants of the delphinium family, so they are bloomers in the sense of plants that flower.

clue.text: Fatuous, trendy leads in awful Netflix entertainment

indicators.note: leads are the front runners, so only the opening letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: in means fashionable
the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses fashionable streaming shows as silly and awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly and lacking sense, a synonym of fatuous.

clue.text: Harry Potter to miss seeing experts?

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and push about, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The boy wizard Harry Potter, famous for his glasses, is going to miss an eye test.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Potter reads as a single name, but Harry is a verb signalling the anagram and only Potter joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Optometrists test eyesight and prescribe glasses, so they are specialists in vision, playfully called seeing experts.
